statement: Get tests whether the ping function is set without holding c.mu.
Release sets the ping function to nil while holding c.mu.
Ping calls c.ping without checking that it is non-nil.
Get blocks on a receive from its request channel with no timeout or cancellation.
Get returns ErrMaxActiveConnReached only when the request channel is closed.
The field waitTimeOut is declared in channelPool.
Close lowers openingConns before it calls the close callback.
Close calls the user close callback while c.mu is held.
Get calls the factory while c.mu is held.
Close returns nil without lowering openingConns when c.close is nil.
Put on a pool whose conns is nil delegates to Close.
Put hands the connection to the oldest waiting request.
The handed-over connection is stamped with the current time.
Put stores the connection in the idle channel with a non-blocking send.
When the idle channel is full Put closes the connection through Close.
Release calls the saved close callback for each idle connection after releasing the lock.
The capacity validation does not require MaxCap to be positive.
NewChannelPool presets openingConns to InitialCap before filling the pool.
NewChannelPool calls Release when the factory fails during the pre-fill.
The pre-fill stores each new connection in the idle channel.
Get ignores the result of Close when it discards an expired idle connection.
A second Release returns early when conns is already nil.
Len returns the number of entries in the idle channel.
Get takes one snapshot of the idle channel at its start.
On the waiter path Get checks the idle timeout and does not call ping.
Get tests for a nil factory only after the openingConns >= maxActive test.
Get queues a waiter when openingConns has reached maxActive.
The Config comment describes InitialCap as the minimum number of connections.
